new_statements.quote: [p.52] Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of full lexical roots [§6.1.1.1]. Stress is not affected by the addition of affixes, or by extrametrical enclitics such as the phrase-level plural marker /-ro/ [§5.4.1.4], or the paragogic /e/ [§5.4.1.7]. [p.58] Stress never occurs on the final (S1) syllable. [p.40] While structurally (phonology, morphology, syntax), Lisela is almost identical with Masarete and Rana, it is the differences in the lexicon that make it marginal for intelligibility purposes.

new_statements.rule_in_words: In Buru (all dialects, Lisela included by the author) word stress is on the penultimate syllable of the lexical root/stem; consonantal enclitics (-k, -t, -n, -h) and the syllabic plural enclitic -ro and paragogic -e are extrametrical and do not move it; the syllabic suffix -i does move stress to the new penult (hefá-i-k); proclitics and cliticised (final-syllable-dropped) roots are unstressed satellites of the following root; phrase stress falls on the last stressed syllable of the phrase.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only remark: the vocative enclitic -é takes primary stress and length, leaving the root's normal penult with secondary stress (p.80 sec.5.8); cliticised root + root compounds show two levels of prominence (p.53).
new_statements.exceptions: Suffix -i shifts stress to the new penultimate (p.54 sec.5.2.3); vocative -é attracts stress (p.80); recent loans follow Ambonese Malay shapes (p.80 sec.5.9). Sec.5.10 lists Lisela's phonetic differences (retained stop+/s/ clusters for Masarete /c/, higher default [e]) with no stress difference.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated on the lexical root / phonological word (stress group), with phrase stress described separately (p.53). The description rests mainly on the Masarete dialect ('Unless otherwise specified, the examples in this study are from the Masarete dialect', p.5); Lisela is covered as one of five Buru dialects, with about a month of Lisela fieldwork and an explicit statement that its phonology is almost identical to Masarete/Rana.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding source (Grimes 1991) is a grammar of Buru (buru1303, ISO mhs) whose examples are Masarete dialect unless stated; it treats Lisela (lise1239, lcl; = Li Enyorot, Wallace's/Hersri's 'Wayapo', Holle list 55c) as one of five Buru dialects, collected Lisela data in Wae Mangit, Wamlana, Silewa and Wae Haa Sa Nangan, and states that Lisela phonology is 'almost identical with Masarete and Rana', listing its only phonetic differences in sec.5.10 (none prosodic). So the penultimate-stress statement applies to Lisela by the author's explicit dialect scope rather than from a Lisela-specific prosodic description. ISO/Glottolog split Lisela off as a separate language mainly on lexical/intelligibility grounds (Grimes 2000 calls it 'marginal').
